after: Stem I ([Preterit nicht belegt]/makəx): 1: (mit ruḥo) sich demütigen, sich bescheiden

new_senses.rationale: Two finite makəx ruḥe clauses contrast with arrogance and parallel lowering the shoulder. A provisional I entry under the assigned root mkk is supported; no unattested nonreflexive meaning or Preterit is reconstructed.

added_examples.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Əno i širayḏi, latyo təm mede! U nošo d lowe əšmo makixo, makəx ruḥe, ṭowər u ġərur...
added_examples.translation: Father Brahim: My advice, there is nothing else! Unless a person is somewhat humble, humbles himself, breaks his arrogance...
added_examples.rationale: First finite example for the new root: overt ruḥe and contrast with arrogance distinguish self-humbling from mere lexical adjective makixo.

added_examples.turoyo: Xori Brahim: U darmono du ġərur i makixuṯo yo. E gabo mənayye d ləm makəx ruḥe, d lə manḥət katfo lu ḥreno, zaṭan gədfayši hawxa, hul d kətne saġ.
added_examples.translation: Father Brahim: The medicine for arrogance is humility. Yes, a side among them that does not humble itself, that does not lower its shoulder to the other, they will just remain like this as long as they are alive.
added_examples.rationale: Second finite example for the new root: negative reflexive clause parallel to lowering one’s shoulder to another; confirms the construction.
